newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Sierra Leone peace talks resume.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone peace talks resume.

text.p: A second round of peace talks between Sierra Leone's military rulers and their West African neighbours began in Abidjan on Tuesday, officials said.
The talks, involving a committee of foreign ministers from regional giant Nigeria, Ghana, Guinea and host Ivory Coast, had been planned for last Friday.

Nigerian Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi, who heads the four-member ministerial committee, said he expected the meeting to come up with a statement on how to build on an agreement that civilian rule should be restored in Sierra Leone.
"We intend to build on progress made at the last meeting," he said. "We expect to make a report to the chairman of ECOWAS (Nigeria's president Sani Abacha)."
Diplomats said earlier that the talks had been put back to allow Sierra Leone's ruling junta more time to meet the committee's demand for the restoration of ousted president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
Soldiers toppled Kabbah on May 25. Rebels, who took up arms in 1991 but agreed peace last November, rallied to the coup.
West African foreign ministers decided in Guinea on June 26 to use dialogue and economic sanctions to persuade the junta to reinstate Kabbah, but they retained a military option.

A statement after July 18 talks in the Ivorian commercial capital Abidjan said the two sides agreed to "resolve all issues related to the Sierra Leone crisis peacefully" and would "work towards early restoration of constitutional order".
They agreed an immediate nationwide truce.
